description:
The crate's in-module tests build their repository from a fixture that declares a taxonomy explicitly, so none of them depends on the binary supplying one.

## Background

Sixty-four call sites across the workspace construct a repository through the scaffold's default hierarchy template and then assert on the type names it wrote. Those assertions hold today because the binary supplies a taxonomy. They stop holding when it does not, and the change that removes it would otherwise carry a workspace-wide fixture rewrite in the same diff as a deletion — two changes that cannot be reviewed against each other.

This covers the crate's in-module tests, where the shared test-utility module already lives, so the fixture is authored here and the other suites adopt it. The call sites are enumerated rather than counted: the archive, initialization, validation, gate-check, profile, graph and config command modules, the JSON storage module, the repository validation module, and the dogfood module. The template module's own call sites are deliberately excluded — they test the type that is being deleted and go with it.

Afterwards each test states the taxonomy it needs, which is also what it should have been doing: a test asserting that a strategic type resolves is testing the mechanism, not the vocabulary.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: One fixture in the shared test-utility module builds a repository whose configuration declares a type hierarchy and the namespaces its consumers assert on.
- [hard] REQ-02: Every in-module test in the enumerated modules that asserts on a type name or a namespace builds its repository through that fixture.
- [hard] REQ-03: An in-module test that needs only a repository, and asserts on no vocabulary, is left alone.
- [hard] REQ-04: The fixture declares its vocabulary in the test rather than reading it from any shipped default, so it holds whether or not the binary supplies one.
- [hard] REQ-05: The suite passes unchanged, since nothing about the code under test changes.

## Notes

The fixture's vocabulary is the suite's own, chosen for the assertions that read it, and deliberately not a copy of what any package declares.
title: Give the crate's own tests a fixture that declares its taxonomy
